title: Understanding N-gram Encoding
text: N-gram encoding captures sequences of letters in a string. Consider how this might affect the representation of DNA sequences.

title: Non-consecutive Segments
text: Think about whether N-gram encoding includes non-consecutive segments of letters and how that might affect the data representation.

title: Meaningless Segments
text: Consider if N-gram encoding captures segments that are too short to have biological meaning.

title: Overlapping Segments
text: Reflect on whether overlapping segments are included in N-gram encoding and how this might affect the data.

title: Evaluating N-gram Encoding
text: Which of the following statements are true about the limitations of N-gram encoding for DNA sequences?
choices: >Overlapping segments would be included, meaning ATGCA is broken up into $$3$$ overlapping words.
>Segments with $$1$$ or $$2$$ letters have no meaning, which $$N-gram$$ would capture as 'words'.
Segments of $$non-consecutive$$ letters would be included, meaning ATGCA could suggest the word AGA.
